tagline: Link payment bugs to Linear and prioritize issues by revenue impact
metaTitle: Linear + Stripe Integration: Payment Failures to Linear Bugs
metaDescription: Open Linear issues when Stripe payment failures spike and add revenue impact to bugs. GAIA helps you rank fixes. See the setup steps.
intro:
Payment failures and billing edge cases discovered in Stripe often lack a clear path to the engineering team. A spike in failed charges that surfaces in the dashboard requires someone to notice it, decide it is an engineering problem, find the right Linear team, and create an issue with enough context to act on. That chain of manual steps means payment issues sit unresolved longer than they should.

GAIA connects Stripe to Linear so payment-related engineering issues are created automatically with full financial context. When a spike in payment failures, a webhook error, or a subscription lifecycle issue is detected, GAIA creates an issue with the event data, affected customer count, and estimated revenue impact so engineers can prioritize it accurately.

This integration is most valuable for SaaS companies where payment reliability is directly tied to revenue and where engineering prioritization should reflect the business impact of technical issues.

useCases.title: Create Linear issues from Stripe payment failure spikes
useCases.description: When the failure rate for a given payment method or error code exceeds a configurable threshold, GAIA creates a high-priority issue with the error breakdown, affected customer count, and estimated revenue at risk.

useCases.title: Link Stripe webhook failures to bugs
useCases.description: When repeated webhook delivery failures to your endpoint are reported, GAIA creates a bug with the failing event types, response codes, and a timeline of failures so engineering can diagnose and resolve the integration issue quickly.

useCases.title: Attach revenue impact to existing payment issues
useCases.description: For issues already tagged with a payment label, GAIA queries Stripe for related error events and attaches an estimated revenue impact figure derived from the affected customers' MRR so product teams can prioritize by business value.

useCases.title: Alert engineering when disputes spike
useCases.description: When dispute volume exceeds a weekly threshold, GAIA creates an investigation issue with a breakdown of the dispute reasons and amounts so the engineering team can identify whether a code change caused the increase.

useCases.title: Close issues when payment errors resolve
useCases.description: When a payment error pattern that triggered an issue returns to baseline, GAIA adds a resolution comment to it and moves it to Done automatically so resolved payment issues do not linger in the backlog.

howItWorks.step: Connect Stripe and Linear to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Stripe account and Linear workspace. Configure the event types and error thresholds that should trigger issue creation.

howItWorks.step: Set revenue impact thresholds and routing rules
howItWorks.description: Define the minimum failure rate or revenue impact that warrants an issue, which team should receive payment issues, and how customer data should be summarized in issue descriptions.

howItWorks.step: Payment issues surface with business context
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors payment events and creates issues automatically when thresholds are crossed. Engineers see the financial impact of payment bugs in their issue tracker and can prioritize accordingly.

faqs.question: Does GAIA include customer PII from Stripe in Linear issues?
faqs.answer: No. GAIA is configured to exclude personally identifiable information by default. Issues receive aggregate statistics — affected customer count, total revenue at risk, error code distribution — without individual customer names, emails, or payment details.

faqs.question: Can GAIA distinguish between transient errors and persistent bugs?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA applies a configurable time-window filter so single transient errors do not create issues. An issue is created only when error rates persist above your threshold across a defined window — for example, a 5% failure rate sustained for 10 minutes.

faqs.question: What events does GAIA monitor beyond payment failures?
faqs.answer: GAIA can monitor any webhook event, including subscription lifecycle events, dispute creation, payout failures, and refund spikes. You configure which event types are relevant for your engineering team during setup.
